target_customer: Independent barbershops and barbers, plus consumers booking cuts
problem: Independent barbershops ran on pen and paper or on software built for other industries, with poor booking, payments and client retention.
business_model: SaaS subscription plus payment processing take rate, with a consumer discovery marketplace
product_category: vertical SaaS and payments for barbershops

founders.name: Songe LaRon
founders.background_notes: YC launch post (Sept 2016) says he went to barbershops with his dad at age six. A 2021 Forbes headline cited on the YC page calls the founders a corporate lawyer and a finance professional, not opened.

founders.name: Dave Salvant
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and president on the YC page and in the Series C release.

founders.name: Yas Tabasam
founders.background_notes: Named alongside LaRon in the YC launch post https://www.ycombinator.com/blog/squire; the post says a person named Dave recruited him. Not listed on the YC company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, payments and later POS, payroll and inventory integration are standard engineering with payments compliance; the founders also ran a shop to test the admin system.

defensibility.rationale: Shops embed bookings, client history and payments; the consumer marketplace adds weak network effects, but generic salon software can copy features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC post says salons used software built for other industries. No incumbent copied it in sources found; the company later reported 6,200+ shops and $3.8B+ processed.

market_need_then: YC launch post Sept 2016: independent shops used pen and paper; high-end shops used software designed for other industries; barbers had large Instagram followings but no booking tools.

branding.name_origin: One article found in search reported the name as a Game of Thrones homage, squires serving knights the way the product serves barbers; not verified against a primary source.

identity.voice_and_tone: practical and barber-first, for example 'Your shop, your clients, your name on the door' on the site

branding.community_and_virality: Waived fees for clients during the pandemic; investors included Stephen Curry, Trevor Noah, Quincy Jones and Pharrell Williams per the Series C release.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct vertical identity and celebrity backers, but no evidence the name itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Squire built vertical software for barbershops, launched in New York in January 2016, and grew through the 2020 reopening, raising a $34M Series B and a $59M Series C at a reported $250M valuation in 2020, and a later round at a reported $750M in 2021. It reports 6,200+ shops, 13M+ appointments and $3.8B+ processed. Success reflects a neglected vertical, founders who ran a shop to learn the trade, and payments revenue.
notes: Competition empty: the YC launch post names none and the only dated competitors found (Booksy, Vagaro, Schedulicity) came from 2026 comparison pages. A 2021 round at a reported $750M valuation (Fortune headline Jul 2021, led by Tiger Global per TechCrunch headline) is not recorded as a round because amount conflicts across outlets ($60M vs $80M) and I did not open those articles. Series C release says $44M equity plus $15M debt while TechCrunch says $45M equity; the release body also conflicts on cumulative totals ($93M this year vs $105M since inception); TechCrunch says valuation about $250M from about $85M in June 2020. Founding year: YC page and release say 2015; TechCrunch says 2016. Squire page lists 150 employees.
